updates.name: Alexander Cede
updates.bio: DSCOVR Scientist at NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, there since 2002, with a University of Innsbruck PhD on ground-based ozone and UV measurements. He designs and calibrates remote sensing instruments and writes trace gas retrieval algorithms. He co-invented the Pandora spectrometer, is technical lead of the NASA-ESA Pandonia Global Network and is PI of NASA's EPIC Level 1 calibration project.
updates.research_interests: remote sensing instrument design and calibration; trace gas column retrieval algorithms; ground-based air quality monitoring; satellite trace gas validation; DSCOVR EPIC calibration
updates.current_affiliation: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, Heliospheric Physics Laboratory (employer listed as SciGLOB Instruments LLC)
updates.evidence: He is co-inventor of the Pandora spectrometer system
updates.notes: Pandora team page (pandora.gsfc.nasa.gov/About/html/team.html, 200) lists 'Alexander Cede Pandora Cofounder Luftblick/NASA GSFC'. NASA SED profile names him Alexander Michael Cede and describes him as technical lead of the Pandonia Global Network, matching the work list. ORCID 0000-0001-7905-3954 (name Alexander Cede) has no employment, works context or profile link, so it was not recorded. luftblick.at and pandonia-global-network.org pages name no individuals (org chart is an image). updates.name: David M. Giles
updates.bio: Senior research scientist with Science Systems and Applications, Inc. at NASA Goddard Space Flight Center. He supported AERONET on site for over twenty years, leading a team that automated cloud screening and near-real-time quality control of aerosol optical depth and developing aerosol type classification methods, then served as science lead of the Atmosphere Observing System Science Data Segment.
updates.research_interests: aerosol remote sensing; aerosol optical depth under anomalous conditions; aerosol, cloud, convection and precipitation algorithms; science data processing systems; machine learning for Earth observations
updates.current_affiliation: Science Systems and Applications, Inc. at NASA Goddard Space Flight Center (Terrestrial Information Systems, Code 619)
updates.evidence: Dr. David Giles has worked on site at the NASA Goddard Space Flight Center for over two decades in support of the Aerosol Robotic Network

updates.name: Alex Webster
updates.bio: Assistant professor of biology at the University of New Mexico and an ecosystem ecologist. She studies how ecosystems and social-ecological systems cope with growing water scarcity and shifting hydrology, working in freshwater systems, watersheds and water infrastructure from desert cities to subarctic forests, and draws on large datasets to test ideas about resilience, connectivity and sustainability.
updates.research_interests: ecosystem and social-ecological resilience to water scarcity; changing hydrologic regimes; freshwater and riparian ecology; watersheds and water infrastructure; climate and land-use change
updates.notes: Homepage on file (alexjwebster.weebly.com) now serves unrelated Swedish-language blog posts, not this person's site; replaced with the UNM Biology profile, which also links her lab site websterlab.weebly.com (200). The profile states she/her and links ORCID 0000-0002-0908-4293 (same as lake) and Google Scholar user=U9mhMtUAAAAJ. pub.orcid.org record: Alex Webster, UNM Biology Assistant Professor from 2023.

updates.name: Andy Schuler
updates.bio: Professor of Civil, Construction and Environmental Engineering at the University of New Mexico and a registered professional engineer in New Mexico. His research centers on biological breakdown of contaminants to protect water quality, including biofilm treatment of nutrients and trace organics such as pharmaceuticals, microbial fuel cell electrodes, competition among wastewater bacteria and agent-based models of microbes.
updates.research_interests: wastewater energy recovery; biofilm-based contaminant removal; removal of nutrients and trace organic pollutants; microbial storage compounds; solids separation; agent-based modeling; molecular study of microbial communities

updates.name: Caroline Scruggs
updates.bio: Regents' Professor of Community and Regional Planning in UNM's School of Architecture and Planning, focused on environmental planning and affiliated with the Water Resources Program. An environmental engineer by training (Virginia Tech) with a Stanford PhD, Scruggs applies mixed-methods, interdisciplinary research on chemicals policy, water scarcity and potable water reuse to inform ecosystem and public health policy.

updates.name: Claudia Pratesi
updates.bio: Assistant professor and MPH program director in the University of New Mexico College of Population Health. Her interdisciplinary work in environmental health and environmental epidemiology examines environmental exposures such as microplastic pollution alongside health disparities, social determinants of health and equity for underserved groups. She earned a doctorate in health sciences at the University of Brasilia.
updates.research_interests: environmental health; environmental epidemiology; One Health and planetary health; population health; health equity

updates.name: Emily Jones
updates.bio: Professor and UNM Regents' Lecturer in Anthropology at the University of New Mexico, on the faculty since 2012, who directs the Zooarchaeology Lab. Research spans past human-environment interaction, historical biogeography, zooarchaeology and domestication, with projects on horses in the Americas, the Columbian exchange in central New Mexico and animals in the Ancestral Pueblo world.

updates.name: Laura Crossey
updates.bio: UNM Distinguished Professor in Earth and Planetary Sciences, on the faculty since 1985 and a past department chair. Her research covers geomicrobiology, low-temperature geochemistry and interactions between water and rock, including how geology shapes water quality, with fieldwork on springs and travertines in the western US, Australia, Egypt and Tibet. She is also a Mars Science Laboratory ChemCam collaborator.
updates.research_interests: aqueous and sedimentary geochemistry; hydrochemistry; diagenesis; geomicrobiology; planetary geology; geothermal processes
